At the next dinner bell, you return to the long table and take an open chair across from Seraphel. Tonight’s meal is less formal: lamb stew, charred squash, coarse bread, and bowls of sharp green herbs passed hand to hand.

Conversation moves between the first day’s instructors and Lucan Aer’s disputed final step in the octagon. When a pause opens, you address Seraphel.

“Do you know a song worth learning?”

She sets down her spoon.

“‘Lanterns on the Low Road’ is easy and bright;  
It’s sung by late travelers walking at night.

“The verses work well with one singer alone,  
But voices join in when the chorus is known.”

Caelindra looks up from her stew. “The fourth verse rhymes *road* with *road*.”

Seraphel turns toward her.

“One traveler walks while the second one rode;  
The spelling repeats, but they differ in mode.”

“That defense makes it worse.”

“Teach him the tavern version,” Ashara says. “It has better rhymes.”

Aldric’s expression becomes precise. “It also has three obscenities.”

“Memorable obscenities.”

Seraphel looks back to you.

“The tavern refrain is both shorter and worse;  
Would you rather start there, or learn the first verse?”
